mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals supply-side disruptions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to potential production shortfalls.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 2% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is cut and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) combined with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a contraction in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines and UNRATE rises, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a high level of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs increase and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 2%, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.
